s: What is JNPA's share in the SPV building Vadhavan Port?
x: JNPA holds 74% and the Maharashtra Maritime Board 26%; Vadhavan is in Palghar, with a 2034 target.

s: New Mangalore port is in which State?
x: New Mangalore is in Karnataka; Kochi is in Kerala and V.O. Chidambaranar in Tamil Nadu.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the order of west-coast ports from north to south?
x: From north to south the order is Deendayal, Mumbai, Mormugao, Kochi, so Kochi lies south of Mormugao.

s: How many major ports does India have (approved total)?
x: India has 13 major ports (12 operational) and about 200 non-major ports.

s: Which major port is India’s first 100 per cent landlord major port and the largest container port?
x: Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA), also known as Nhava Sheva, is India’s largest container port and its first 100 per cent landlord major port.

s: Which was the first major port on the east coast established after Independence (declared on 18 April 1966)?
x: Paradip was declared a major port on 18 April 1966, the first major port on the east coast established after Independence.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a west-coast major port of India?
x: Paradip is in Odisha on the east coast, in the Mahanadi delta. Mormugao (Goa) is a west-coast major port. New Mangalore (Karnataka) and Kochi (Kerala) are west-coast major ports too.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Deendayal Port — Gujarat, Gulf of Kachchh, west coast
Kochi Port — Tamil Nadu, east coast
Paradip Port — Andhra Pradesh, east coast
x: Deendayal Port is in Gujarat on the Gulf of Kachchh on the west coast. Mumbai is in Maharashtra, Kochi is in Kerala, and Paradip is in Odisha.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Kochi — Natural port on Vembanad Lake
Chennai — Natural harbour on Salsette Island
Visakhapatnam — Artificial all-weather harbour north of Adam’s Bridge
Tuticorin — Deepest landlocked port called the “Brightest Jewel”
x: Kochi is a natural port on Vembanad Lake. Salsette Island is associated with Mumbai, the artificial all-weather harbour north of Adam’s Bridge is Tuticorin, and the “Brightest Jewel” is Visakhapatnam.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kamarajar — India's first corporatised major port
V.O. Chidambaranar — Artificial all-weather deep-sea harbour north of Adam's Bridge
Paradip — Oldest artificial port of the east coast
x: Chennai, not Paradip, is the oldest artificial port of the east coast; Paradip, in the Mahanadi delta, was commissioned in 1966.

s: Which of the following harbour–State pairs is correctly matched?
x: Udupi (Malpe) is in Karnataka. Janjira is in Maharashtra, Kochi in Kerala and Kakinada in Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which of the following port–State pairs is correctly matched?
x: Kamarajar is in Tamil Nadu. Visakhapatnam is in Andhra Pradesh, Haldia in West Bengal and Paradip in Odisha.

s: Which of the following port–State pairs is correctly matched?
x: Mormugao is in Goa. Mumbai is in Maharashtra, Paradip in Odisha and Kamarajar (Ennore) in Tamil Nadu.

s: Mormugao port lies at the mouth of which river?
x: Mormugao is at the Zuari mouth; Paradip is in the Mahanadi–Bay of Bengal region and Dahej on the Gulf of Khambhat.

s: Kamarajar Port is the present name of which port?
x: Kamarajar is Ennore; V.O. Chidambaranar is Tuticorin and Kolkata is Syama Prasad Mukherjee Port.

s: With the export of which of the following is New Mangalore Port mainly associated?
x: New Mangalore Port in Karnataka exports Kudremukh iron ore. The other minerals and regions are not the speciality stated for this port.

s: Which of the following is a west-coast harbour?
x: Kochi (like Mumbai) is on the west coast; Haldia and Paradip are on the east coast.

s: Which is India's oldest and biggest artificial port?
x: Chennai (1881) is the oldest and biggest artificial port; Mumbai is the largest natural port.

s: Kandla port was developed in the 1950s mainly to make up for the loss of which port after Partition?
x: After Partition Karachi went to Pakistan, so Kandla was built on the Gulf of Kutch to serve western India.

s: In which district of Maharashtra is Vadhavan, India's 13th major port, being built?
x: Vadhavan port is being built in Palghar district by an SPV of JNPA (74%) and Maharashtra Maritime Board (26%).

s: Near the mouth of which river is Paradip port located?
x: Paradip, Odisha's major port, lies at the Mahanadi delta and exports iron ore to Japan.

s: In which year was the Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva) commissioned?
x: JNPA at Nhava Sheva was commissioned in 1989 to ease congestion at Mumbai port.

s: In which State is the Haldia port located?
x: Haldia is part of the Kolkata-Haldia port, India's only riverine major port, in West Bengal.

s: Which one of the following is the only riverine major port of India?
x: Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port, comprising Kolkata-Haldia, is the oldest major port and the only riverine major port of India. It is situated on the Hooghly.

s: Which major port handled the highest import tonnage in 2023-24?
x: Deendayal (Kandla) port in Gujarat led in import tonnage in 2023-24.

s: Which of the following is a tidal port of India?
x: Kandla (Deendayal) on the Gulf of Kutch is a tidal port; Chennai is artificial and Mumbai is natural.

s: The SUMED pipeline in Egypt connects Ain Sukhna on the Red Sea with which place?
x: SUMED runs from Ain Sukhna to Sidi Kerir on the Mediterranean, carrying Gulf oil towards Europe.

s: Bab-el-Mandeb connects the Red Sea with which water body?
x: Bab-el-Mandeb, between Yemen and Djibouti/Eritrea, links the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden; Suez links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.

s: Which chokepoint was reported closed in early March 2026 during the US–Israel war on Iran?
x: The Strait of Hormuz was reported closed in early March 2026 during the US–Israel war on Iran.

s: After the Houthis took Perim Island in September 2026, traffic was disrupted through:
x: After the Houthis took Perim Island, traffic through both Hormuz and Bab-el-Mandeb was reported disrupted in September 2026.

s: Which one of the following statements about the Panama Canal is correct?
o: It connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea and was completed in 1914.
It connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, uses a lock system and was completed in 1914.
It connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans without any locks and was completed in 1945.
It connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and uses a lock system.
x: Option B is correct: the Panama Canal links the Atlantic and Pacific through a lock system and was completed in 1914. Option A describes the Suez Canal's connection. Option C is wrong on both the lock system and the year. Option D describes Bab-el-Mandeb.

s: The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea with which water body?
x: Suez links the Mediterranean with the Red Sea; Bab-el-Mandeb then leads to the Gulf of Aden.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Suez Route?
o: It is the shortest route between Europe and Asia
It connects Europe and Asia through the Suez Canal
It goes round the Cape of Good Hope
It avoids the voyage round Africa
x: The Suez Route cuts through the Suez Canal and avoids the trip round Africa; the Cape of Good Hope route is the one round Africa.

s: Which of the following sea route – link pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Panama Canal Route – Atlantic and Pacific
Cape of Good Hope Route – Europe and Asia via the Suez Canal
Trans-Pacific Route – East Asia and the West Coast of the Americas
Mediterranean–Indian Ocean Route – Europe and Asia/East Africa via the Suez Canal
x: The Cape route links Europe and Asia by going round southern Africa, not through Suez.

s: Which strait is an alternative to the Strait of Malacca?
x: The Lombok (or Sunda) Strait is the alternative to Malacca.

s: Which straits make up the Turkish Straits linking the Black Sea and the Mediterranean?
x: The Bosphorus and Dardanelles form the Turkish Straits, giving Russia warm-water access.

s:
Assertion (A): The Strait of Hormuz is the most critical oil chokepoint.
Reason (R): About 20% of global oil passes through the Strait of Hormuz.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: carrying about 20% of global oil is what makes Hormuz the most critical oil chokepoint.

s: Which of the following is the busiest sea route in the world and is also called the “Big Trunk Route”?
x: The North Atlantic Route, the Big Trunk Route, is the busiest sea route, linking the US north-east and north-west Europe.

s: Which waterway, linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, shortens the Europe–Asia route by up to 7,000 km?
x: The Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea and shortens the Europe–Asia route by up to 7,000 km, giving it the greatest economic and strategic significance.

s: The Strait of Malacca lies between the Malay Peninsula and which island?
x: The Strait of Malacca separates the Malay Peninsula from Sumatra and links the Andaman Sea with the South China Sea.

s: Which two water bodies does the Strait of Hormuz connect?
o: Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman
Red Sea and Gulf of Aden
Arabian Sea and Gulf of Aden
x: The Strait of Hormuz links the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman; about 20% of world oil passes through it.

s: In which year was the Suez Canal opened?
x: The Suez Canal in Egypt opened in 1869; the Panama Canal opened in 1914.

s: What is the length of the Suez Canal?
x: The Suez Canal in Egypt is 193.30 km long and links the Mediterranean with the Red Sea; Panama Canal is about 82 km.

s: What was the value of India's rice exports in FY 2026?
x: Rice exports were US$ 11.53 billion, down 7.5%; electronics exports topped US$ 40 billion.

s: Which country is the leading exporter of palm oil?
x: Indonesia leads palm-oil exports, followed by Malaysia.

s: Which country has the world's largest area under cotton cultivation?
x: India has the largest area under cotton, though its yields are lower than China's.

s: Which one of the following was India's leading merchandise export item in 2024–25?
x: Petroleum products were the largest listed export item, accounting for 14.48% of exports in 2024–25.

s: In FY 2025, which export category was the third largest for India?
x: Electronics was India's third-largest export category in FY 2025, after engineering goods and petroleum products.

s: What is India's rank in world pharmaceutical exports by volume?
x: India is third in pharma exports by volume, first in rice and seventh in refined petroleum.

s: Which one of the following is classified as a bulk import of India?
x: Bulk imports include petroleum, cereals and pulses, edible oils, sugar, fertilizer, metals and ores. Capital goods, precious products, plastics and chemicals are non-bulk imports.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with India's import dependence?
x: India's import dependence is about 88–89% for crude oil, 47–51% for natural gas and 26% for coal.

s: Which country is the largest producer of jute?
x: India is the largest jute producer; Bangladesh is a major competitor, important in raw-jute exports.

s: Which one of the following is NOT an import item of India, India being an exporter of it?
x: India exports iron ore rather than importing it (APPSC 2018). Crude petroleum, gold and edible oils are major imports.

s: Of which of the following is India the largest producer, consumer and exporter?
x: India leads in spices; in pulses it is the largest producer and consumer but also an importer.

s: Which was India's top merchandise import in FY 2024-25?
x: Crude petroleum is India's largest import, with 88-89% import dependence; gold and silver come next.

s: Which country is the world's largest exporter of sugar?
x: Brazil leads world sugar exports, followed by India.

s: Which country is the largest exporter of gold to India?
x: Switzerland, a gold refining hub, is the largest exporter of gold to India.

s: Which country was the largest destination of India's exports in 2024–25?
x: The USA took 19.77%, ahead of the UAE (8.37%), UK (3.32%) and China (3.26%).

s: How did the UAE's share in India's exports change?
x: The UAE's share fell from 8.5% to 6.5%, while China's rose from 3.3% to 4.4% and Singapore's from 2.7% to 4.7%.

s: About what share of India's LPG imports comes from West Asia?
x: About 90% of India's LPG imports (and more than 40% of crude oil imports) come from West Asia.

s: Which one of the following represents the correct order of India’s leading import sources?
o: China, UAE, Russia, USA and Iraq
USA, China, UAE, Iraq and Russia
UAE, China, USA, Russia and Iraq
Russia, China, Iraq, UAE and USA
x: China was the largest import source for India, followed by the UAE, Russia, the USA and Iraq.

s: Trade with China through which passes has been suspended since 2020?
o: Nathu La, Zoji La and Bomdi La
Khardung La, Chang La and Bara-Lacha La
Lipulekh, Shipki La and Nathu La
x: China-border trade through Lipulekh, Shipki La and Nathu La has been suspended since 2020.

s: Which country was India's top crude oil supplier in 2025?
x: Russia was the top crude supplier in 2025; Saudi Arabia led earlier and Iraq in 2017-18.

s: After Independence, towards which country did India's trade first shift away from the UK and Western Europe?
x: Trade moved towards the US and later towards Asia (China, UAE, ASEAN).

s: Coastal shipping in India grew by approximately what percentage over a decade?
x: Coastal shipping grew by 118% over a decade.

s: Ports carry approximately what share of India’s trade by volume and by value, respectively?
x: Ports carry about 95% of India’s trade by volume and 68% by value.

s: As per the 2024 recalculation, what is the length of India's coastline?
x: The 2024 recalculation put India's coastline at about 11,098 km; 7,517 km was the earlier figure.

s: Vizhinjam, India's first dedicated international transshipment port, is in which State?
x: Vizhinjam is in Kerala and is now also a customs port.

s: Which of the following describes the eastern coastal plain of India?
o: Narrow, lying between the Arabian Sea and the Western Ghats
Confined to the Kaveri delta alone
x: The east coast is broad and deltaic (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri); the narrow west coast lies between the Arabian Sea and the Western Ghats.

s: The Dhamra LNG terminal is in which State?
x: Dhamra is in Odisha; Ennore is in Tamil Nadu, Mundra in Gujarat and Dabhol in Maharashtra.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding India’s ports is correct?
o: Non-major ports are governed exclusively by the Major Port Authorities Act.
All ports are governed by the Major Port Authorities Act.
Major ports are governed by State Maritime Boards, while non-major ports are governed by the Union Government.
Major ports are governed by the Major Port Authorities Act, while non-major ports fall under State Maritime Boards.
x: The 13 major ports are governed by the Major Port Authorities Act, while about 200 non-major ports are administered under State Maritime Boards.

s: Which state has the longest coastline?
x: Gujarat has India's longest coastline, with Kathiawar and Kutch.

s: Which port led in liquid-bulk cargo in the port performance index?
x: Sikka led liquid bulk; Paradip led dry bulk, while Mundra and JNPA led in container cargo.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Kolkata is the only riverine major port.
Chennai is one of the oldest artificial ports of India.
Mumbai is the largest privately owned port.
Visakhapatnam is India’s deepest port and a natural port.
x: Option C is incorrect: Mundra in Gujarat, not Mumbai, is the largest privately owned port; Mumbai is a major port under the Union. Kolkata, Chennai and Visakhapatnam are rightly described.

s: The Dabhol LNG terminal is in which State?
x: Dabhol is in Maharashtra; Dahej is in Gujarat, Dhamra in Odisha and Kochi in Kerala.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the west coast of India?
o: It has a wide shallow shelf with large deltas and few estuaries.
It is a submerged and indented coastline with deep water close to the shore.
It is dominated by cyclones and has no natural harbours.
It receives greater deltaic sediment from the Mahanadi and Godavari.
x: The west coast is submerged and indented, with deep water close to the shore. This favours natural harbours, and estuaries are more common than deltas.

s: Compared with the west coast, how much sediment does the east coast of India receive?
x: The east coast receives more sediment; with cyclones and a wide, shallow shelf, this gives it fewer natural harbours.

s: On which idea is the Sagarmala programme (2015) of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways built?
x: Sagarmala aims at port-led development through pillars such as port modernisation, connectivity and port-led industrialisation.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Sagarmala programme:
1. It was launched in 2015.
2. Port-led industrialisation is one of its pillars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Sagarmala began in 2015 under MoPSW; its five pillars include modernisation, connectivity and industrialisation.

s: Which of the following is NOT a reason for the east coast of India having fewer ports?
o: Deep water close to the shore
x: Deep water near the shore is a feature of the west coast; the east coast is deltaic, shallow, cyclone-prone and sediment-heavy.

s: Which is the world's busiest container port?
x: Shanghai is the busiest; Rotterdam is Europe's largest and Singapore a Malacca-route transshipment hub.

s: Which port is the major global transshipment hub?
x: Singapore, not London, is the global transshipment hub.

s: Which is Europe's largest seaport?
x: Rotterdam is Europe's largest port; Shanghai is the world's busiest container port.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Port) - List-II (Country)
A. Rotterdam 1. Uruguay
B. Busan 2. China
C. Montevideo 3. Netherlands
D. Ningbo 4. South Korea
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Rotterdam is in the Netherlands, Busan in South Korea, Montevideo in Uruguay and Ningbo in China.

s: On which river does the Russian timber-exporting port of Igarka lie?
x: Igarka is a port of Krasnoyarsk Krai in Siberia on the Yenisei river, reached by ocean-going ships and exporting timber.

s: India's FTAs could cover about 75% of its exports, but what is their actual utilisation?
x: India's FTAs could cover approximately 75% of exports, but actual utilisation is only around 20–30%.

s: What binding investment commitment does the India-EFTA TEPA carry?
x: TEPA binds US$ 100 billion over 15 years; it was signed in March 2024 and is in force since 2025.

s: In which year was India's TEPA with the EFTA countries concluded?
x: The India-EFTA TEPA dates from 2024, not 2022 as is often assumed.

s: Which of the following agreements was concluded in 2025?
x: The CEPA with Oman (like the UK CETA) is from 2025; TEPA is 2024 and the UAE CEPA and Australia ECTA are 2022.

s: What was India's trade-agreement count as of June 2026?
o: 14 FTAs covering 6 countries, talks with 27 more
42 FTAs covering 15 countries, talks with 27 more
27 FTAs covering 15 countries, talks with 42 more
15 FTAs covering 27 countries, talks with 42 more
x: In June 2026 India had 15 FTAs covering 27 countries and was in talks with 42 more countries.

s: In which year was SAFTA signed?
x: SAFTA is 2004; SAPTA 1993, the India-ASEAN goods agreement 2009 and India-UAE CEPA 2022.

s: When was the India-UK CETA signed?
x: It was signed on 24 July 2025 and came into force on 15 July 2026; 27 January 2026 is when India-EU FTA talks concluded.

s: Which one of the following agreements provided duty-free access for 90% of Indian exports, with Indian exports rising by 12% in its first year?
x: The India-UAE CEPA, signed in 2022, provided duty-free access for 90% of Indian exports and exports rose by 12% in the first year.

s: The India-EU FTA, described as the “Mother of All Deals”, provides access on approximately what proportion of tariff lines?
x: The India-EU FTA provides access on 97% of tariff lines. The 99.5% figure refers to the proportion of trade value covered, not tariff lines.

s: To what does the US$ 100 bn target under the India-UAE CEPA relate?
x: The UAE CEPA target is US$ 100 bn of trade; the US$ 100 bn commitment of the EFTA TEPA is investment.

s: In which year was the India-ASEAN agreement on trade in goods signed?
x: The India-ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement dates from 2009; SAFTA was 2004.

s: When was the India-EU Free Trade Agreement concluded?
x: The India-EU FTA was concluded on 27 January 2026, covering 97% of tariff lines; 24 July 2025 is the UK CETA signing.

s: Which agreement replaced NAFTA?
x: USMCA replaced NAFTA; Mercosur is Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.

s: Where was the 14th WTO Ministerial Conference (MC14) held in March 2026?
x: MC14 met at Yaounde, Cameroon, 26-29 March 2026; the e-commerce moratorium lapsed on 31 March 2026.

s: With which issue is the WTO coalition NAMA-11 mainly concerned?
x: NAMA-11 is a coalition of developing countries in the WTO dealing with non-agricultural market access; India, Brazil and South Africa are among its members.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a member of SAFTA?
x: SAFTA includes the eight SAARC countries, including Bhutan, Afghanistan and Maldives. Myanmar is not among the listed SAFTA members.

s: In which year did Timor-Leste become the 11th member of ASEAN?
x: Timor-Leste became ASEAN’s 11th member in 2025.

s: Approximately what share of Andhra Pradesh’s exports goes to the RCEP and USMCA blocs together?
x: About 53% of Andhra Pradesh’s exports go to the RCEP and USMCA blocs together.

s: In which year did India stay out of the RCEP?
x: RCEP joins ASEAN with China, Japan, Korea, Australia and New Zealand; India opted out in 2019.

s: Which of the following is NOT a member of Mercosur?
x: Mercosur members are Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay; Chile is not among them.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's export targets?
o: The Export Promotion Mission (2025-26 to 2030-31) is run by DGFT
It works through Niryat Protsahan and Niryat Disha
The Mission targets US$ 2 trillion of goods and services exports by 2030
NITI Aayog's Export Preparedness Index is aligned to US$ 2 trillion of merchandise exports by 2030
x: The EPI is aligned to US$ 1 trillion of merchandise exports by 2030.

s: What was the value of India's merchandise exports in FY 2025-26?
x: India's merchandise exports reached an all-time high of US$ 441.78 billion in FY 2025–26, up 0.93%.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's position in world trade (2024)?
o: India's share in world merchandise exports was 1.8%
India's share in world services exports was 4.3%
x: India ranked 7th in services exports; 18th is its merchandise rank.

s: What was India's record merchandise trade deficit in FY 2025-26?
x: The FY26 deficit was US$ 333.2 billion; US$ 282.5 billion was FY25. CAD was US$ 30.2 billion (1.1% of GDP).

s: Imports of which items mainly drove the rise in India's merchandise imports in FY 2025-26?
x: FY26 merchandise imports of about US$775 bn (up 7.45%) were driven by a jump in gold and silver imports.

s: By about how much did India's exports to the Gulf fall in March 2026 due to the West Asia war?
x: Exports to the Gulf fell by about 57% in March 2026 as a result of the West Asia war.

s: India's current account deficit in FY 2025-26 was about what share of GDP?
x: The CAD was US$ 30.2 bn, about 1.1% of GDP, with services in surplus.

s: What does India's target of US$ 2 trillion exports by 2030 cover?
x: The US$ 2 trillion target is for goods plus services; US$ 1 trillion is the merchandise figure.

s: Under the RBI's July 2022 framework, through which accounts can India's exports and imports be invoiced and settled in rupees?
x: The July 2022 framework permits invoicing and settlement in Indian rupees through Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (SRVAs).

s: How was the rupee made convertible under partial current-account convertibility in 1992?
o: 20% at the official rate and 80% at the market rate
60% at the official rate and 40% at the market rate
40% at the official rate and 60% at the market rate
x: In 1992, 40% of current-account transactions were convertible at the official rate and 60% at the market rate.

s: Which policy characterized India's trade regime during 1950–1990?
o: Import substitution and an inward-looking policy
x: From 1950 to 1990, India followed import substitution through an inward-looking policy lasting approximately four decades.

s: When did the two-step rupee devaluation under the 1991 New Trade Policy take place?
x: The rupee was devalued in two steps in July 1991; the policy also moved to a price-based mechanism and eased import licensing.

s: In which year was FERA replaced by FEMA?
x: FERA was liberalised in 1993 and replaced by FEMA in 1999.

s: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 shifted from export incentives to which approach?
x: FTP 2023 moved from incentives to remission of duties, with ease of exporting and Districts as Export Hubs.

s: Where was Asia's first Export Processing Zone set up in 1965?
x: Kandla EPZ, established in 1965, was Asia's first Export Processing Zone.

s: What US tariff was in force on India while a trade deal with the United States was still under negotiation?
x: A US tariff of 25% plus 25%, amounting to 50%, was in force while the deal remained under negotiation.

s: In which decade did East Asian economies adopt export promotion and move ahead of India?
x: East Asian economies adopted outward-looking export promotion in the 1970s and moved ahead of India.

s: What replaced quantitative restrictions under the 1991 New Trade Policy?
x: The 1991 reforms moved from quantitative restrictions to a price-based mechanism and eased licensing.

s: Sri City, a multi-product zone with SEZ, DTZ, FTWZ and Electronics Manufacturing Cluster components, is in which district?
x: Sri City is in Tirupati district and combines a multi-product SEZ, DTZ, Free Trade Warehousing Zone and Electronics Manufacturing Cluster.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: Kakinada SEZ is located in Kakinada, not Srikakulam district. Pydibhimavaram is the pharma cluster associated with Srikakulam.

s: As of July 2023, how many notified SEZs did Andhra Pradesh have?
x: AP had 32 notified SEZs as of July 2023; 19 refers to operational SEZs around January 2019.

s: How many operational SEZs did Andhra Pradesh have around January 2019?
x: Andhra Pradesh had 19 operational SEZs in the period referred to by the APPSC-GS 2018 key. The notified count in July 2023 was 32.

s: Which is the nodal agency for industrial parks and SEZs in Andhra Pradesh?
x: APIIC is the nodal agency for industrial parks and SEZs in AP and has developed 10 SEZs.

s: Divi's Laboratories, located in the Visakhapatnam region, is associated with which sector?
x: Divi's Laboratories is a pharmaceutical unit in the Visakhapatnam region (with Parawada Pharma City). Apparel is linked to Brandix India Apparel City at Atchutapuram. Electronics manufacturing (Foxconn) is linked to Sri City. Automobiles (Isuzu) are also linked to Sri City.

s: The Pydibhimavaram pharma cluster is in which district?
x: Pydibhimavaram is in Srikakulam; Kakinada SEZ is in Kakinada district.

s: Which of the following SEZ/unit – district pairs is correctly matched?
x: APSEZ is at Atchutapuram-Rambilli in Anakapalli; Kakinada SEZ is in Kakinada, Sri City in Tirupati and Pydibhimavaram in Srikakulam.

s: Brandix Apparel City at Atchutapuram is associated with which sector?
x: Brandix at Atchutapuram is an apparel unit; Foxconn (electronics) and Isuzu (automobiles) are at Sri City.

s: Where is the Isuzu automobile unit in Andhra Pradesh located?
x: Sri City in Tirupati district hosts Isuzu (automobiles) and Foxconn (electronics).

s: In which district is the Jawaharlal Nehru Pharma City at Parawada located?
x: JN Pharma City at Parawada, with units of Divi's, Dr. Reddy's and Aurobindo, is in Anakapalli district.

s: Which is the only major port of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Visakhapatnam is AP's only major port; Krishnapatnam, Kakinada and Gangavaram are non-major ports.

s: Visakhapatnam Port handled a record cargo of about how much in 2025-26?
x: Visakhapatnam handled a record 91.17 MMT in 2025-26, up from 82.62 MMT in 2024-25.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Visakhapatnam Port?
o: It is the only major port of AP
It is 2nd among east-coast major ports
It ranks 1st among all major ports
It handled a record 91.17 MMT in 2025-26
x: Visakhapatnam is 4th among major ports and 2nd on the east coast, not first overall.

s: What is the length of the coastline of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Andhra Pradesh has a coastline of about 1,053 km.

s: Which place in coastal Andhra had the first English factory, set up in 1611?
x: The first English factory in coastal Andhra was at Machilipatnam in 1611. Visakhapatnam, Kakinada and Krishnapatnam are today's port towns, but none of them holds this first.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's rank among India's exporting States in FY 2024-25?
x: AP was the sixth largest exporting State in FY 2024-25, shipping 824 commodities to 194 countries.

s: Which of the following is not an export item of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Crude oil is not an AP export; marine products, pharmaceuticals, food products, textiles and engineering goods are.

s: After bifurcation, Andhra Pradesh turned to port-led development mainly because it:
o: lost its major ports to Telangana
was barred by the SEZ Act from inland industry
x: After bifurcation, Andhra Pradesh lost Hyderabad's industrial clusters and responded by pursuing port-led development.

s: Andhra Pradesh exports 824 commodities to how many countries?
x: AP's export spread is 824 commodities to 194 countries.

s: Which one of the following commodities ranked first for Andhra Pradesh in FY 2024-25 with a 67% share of India's exports?
x: Tobacco ranked first for Andhra Pradesh and accounted for 67% of India's exports in the stated FY 2024-25 data.

s: Which of the following pairs regarding Andhra Pradesh's export rank in FY 2024-25 is correctly matched?
o: Mica, coal and other ores – Third
x: In FY 2024-25 AP ranked first in marine products with a 43% share; it was first in ores, second in coffee and third in spices.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's rank among States in coffee exports?
x: AP is 2nd in coffee and 3rd in spices, while it is 1st in tobacco, marine products and ores.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's rank among States in spices exports?
x: AP is 3rd in spices exports; it is 2nd in coffee.

s: With which refinery are Andhra Pradesh's exports of petroleum products associated?
x: Petroleum product exports come from the Visakhapatnam refinery, not Kurnool.

s: Which shrimp is mainly exported from Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP's shrimp exports are mainly white-leg shrimp, grown chiefly in West Godavari, Krishna and Nellore.

s: Which exports of Andhra Pradesh were mainly hit by the 50% United States tariff?
x: The 50% US tariff was reported to have affected Andhra Pradesh's shrimp sector and aqua exports.

s: From which districts of Andhra Pradesh does most of the State's shrimp export come?
x: White-leg shrimp for export to the US and EU is farmed mainly in West Godavari, Krishna and Nellore.

s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh is known for chilli exports?
x: Guntur is the chilli export hub of Andhra Pradesh.

s: About what share of India's shrimp exports does Andhra Pradesh supply (January 2026)?
x: Andhra Pradesh supplies about 70% of India's shrimp exports.

s: How is a Special Economic Zone treated for trade and tariff purposes?
o: Foreign territory only for income tax
Territory with no special customs treatment
x: An SEZ is treated as foreign territory for trade and tariffs and works through a single-window system.

s: What does the SEZ Act, 2005 seek to do to domestic and foreign investment?
x: Promotion of domestic and foreign investment is an objective of the SEZ Act, along with economic activity, exports, employment and infrastructure.

s: In which year was the SEZ policy announced in India under the EXIM Policy?
x: The SEZ policy was announced in 2000 under the EXIM Policy/Foreign Trade Policy; the SEZ Act followed in 2005.

s: Who can set up an SEZ under the SEZ framework?
o: Only a joint venture of the Centre and a State
The Centre, a State or any person, jointly or severally
x: An SEZ may be established by the Centre, a State or any person, jointly or severally; it is not restricted to government joint ventures.

s: How does an Export Oriented Unit (EOU) differ from an SEZ?
o: A single unit that may be located anywhere under the FTP scheme
A developer-led enclave with its own infrastructure
A demarcated enclave notified under the SEZ Act, 2005
A zone made up of a developer and several units
x: An EOU is a single unit located anywhere under the Foreign Trade Policy scheme; the developer-plus-units enclave belongs to an SEZ.

s: What did the Baba Kalyani Committee (2018) propose to rename Special Economic Zones as?
x: The Baba Kalyani Committee proposed the term “3Es”, meaning Employment and Economic Enclaves, for SEZs.

s: An SEZ proposal goes from the State to which body for approval?
x: SEZ proposals are sent by the State to the Board of Approval.

s: In which year was the Special Economic Zones Act enacted?
x: The SEZ policy came in 2000 under the EXIM Policy; the SEZ Act was passed in 2005.

s: SEZ exports make up about what share of India's exports?
x: SEZ exports of Rs 14.64 lakh crore (about US$ 173 bn) are about 21% of India's exports.

s: In which year was the Export Oriented Unit (EOU) scheme introduced?
x: The EOU scheme came in 1981 under the trade policy; Kandla EPZ was 1965 and the SEZ policy 2000.

s: The AP Retail Trade Policy 2015–20 targeted how many additional retail jobs by 2020?
x: The policy targeted 20,000 additional jobs in the retail sector by 2020.

s: Which of the following is an objective of the Andhra Pradesh Export Promotion Policy (APEX) 2022–27?
o: Integrated export ecosystems from districts to ports
x: APEX 2022–27 promotes global market access, logistics, competitiveness and integrated district-to-port export ecosystems.

s: What export target does AP's Industrial Development Policy 4.0 (2024-29) set?
x: The policy targets US$ 40 billion exports, along with Rs 30 lakh crore investment and 175+ industrial parks.

s: Which organisation is building the Dugarajapatnam shipbuilding cluster under the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Policy?
x: The special purpose vehicle NSHIP-AP Ltd is building the Dugarajapatnam shipbuilding cluster.

s: The Dugarajapatnam shipbuilding cluster under AP's Maritime Policy aims at what share of national capacity by 2047?
x: The cluster built by NSHIP-AP Ltd targets 25% of national shipbuilding capacity by 2047.

s: AP's Industrial Development Policy 4.0 (2024-29) plans how many industrial parks?
x: IDP 4.0 plans 175+ industrial parks, with US$ 40 bn exports and 5 lakh jobs.

s: What investment target does Andhra Pradesh's Industrial Development Policy 4.0 (2024-29) set?
x: IDP 4.0 targets Rs 30 lakh crore investment, 5 lakh jobs and US$ 40 bn exports.

s: Which District Export Hub is correctly matched with its products?
o: Visakhapatnam—marine products, engineering goods and health services
East Godavari—chillies, turmeric and cotton yarn
Guntur—coir products, cashew and nursery plants
Visakhapatnam—coir products, cashew and nursery plants
x: The Phase-I Visakhapatnam District Export Hub covers marine products, engineering goods and health services. East Godavari covers coir, cashew and nursery plants, while Guntur covers chillies, turmeric and cotton yarn.

s: In which year was the Districts as Export Hubs (DEH) initiative launched under the Foreign Trade Policy?
x: DEH was launched in 2019 under the FTP, with DGFT as nodal agency.

s: Which is the nodal agency for the Districts as Export Hubs initiative?
x: DEH, launched in 2019 under the FTP, is run by the DGFT; ODOP was merged into it.

s: Coir, cashew and nursery plants are the DEH Phase-I products of which AP district?
x: East Godavari's products are coir, cashew and nursery plants; Guntur's are chillies, turmeric and cotton yarn.

s: In the Export Preparedness Index 2024, Andhra Pradesh ranked how high among large States?
x: In EPI 2024 (4th edition, released by NITI Aayog in Jan 2026) Andhra Pradesh ranked 5th among large States, after Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh. Ninth was AP's rank in EPI 2021.

s: Andhra Pradesh ranked ninth in which edition of the Export Preparedness Index?
x: Andhra Pradesh ranked 9th in EPI 2021, the second edition (APPSC-GS 2022 key). In EPI 2024 (4th edition) it ranked 5th among large States.

s: With which institution did NITI Aayog prepare the first Export Preparedness Index (2020)?
x: The first EPI, released in 2020, was prepared by NITI Aayog with the Institute for Competitiveness.

s: In NITI Aayog's Export Preparedness Index 2024, which pillar carries the highest weight of 40%?
x: In EPI 2024, Business Ecosystem carries 40%. Export Infrastructure, Policy and Governance, and Export Performance each carry 20%.

s: In LEADS 2024, Andhra Pradesh was placed in which category?
x: AP was an Achiever in 2022 and 2023, a Fast Mover in 2024 and an Accelerator in LEADS 2025.

s: In LEADS 2025, Andhra Pradesh was ranked in which tier among coastal States?
x: LEADS 2025 has four tiers; AP was an Accelerator among coastal States.

s: Which State topped NITI Aayog's Export Preparedness Index 2024?
x: In EPI 2024 the order was Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which body is reviewing the proposal for a dry port at Sri City in Tirupati district?
x: The Sri City dry port proposal in Tirupati district is under review by an Inter-Ministerial Committee.

s: Which is India's first coastal industrial corridor?
x: The Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC) is India's first coastal industrial corridor and part of the East Coast Economic Corridor.

s: Under CBIC guidelines, a new dry port is generally not allowed within how many km of a seaport?
x: The CBIC norm bars a new dry port within 200 km of a seaport; 100 km applies to distance from an ICD.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: VCIC — Visakhapatnam, Chittoor/Srikalahasti-Yerpedu and Kopparthy nodes
ECEC — Orvakal as its only Andhra Pradesh node
x: Orvakal is the node of HBIC. VCIC is part of the ECEC and has the listed Visakhapatnam, Chittoor/Srikalahasti-Yerpedu and Kopparthy nodes; the statement that ECEC has Orvakal as its only AP node is incorrect.

s: Orvakal in Andhra Pradesh is a node of which industrial corridor?
x: Orvakal is a node of the HBIC, not of the VCIC/ECEC.

s: Which of the following is NOT a node of the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor?
x: VCIC nodes are Visakhapatnam, Srikalahasti-Yerpedu and Kopparthy; Orvakal belongs to the HBIC.

s:
Assertion (A): Andhra Pradesh has no UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Reason (R): India has 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites as of July 2026.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both are true: AP has no WHS and India has 45 sites (July 2026), but India's total does not explain AP having none.

s:
Arrange the following UNESCO World Heritage inscriptions in chronological order:
A. Moidams of the Ahom Dynasty
B. Ramappa Temple and Dholavira
C. Maratha Military Landscapes of India
D. Santiniketan and Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas
x: Ramappa and Dholavira (2021), Santiniketan and the Hoysalas (2023), Moidams (2024), Maratha Military Landscapes (2025): B, D, A, C.

s: What do the Maratha Military Landscapes of India, inscribed in 2025, comprise?
o: 12 forts, including 11 in Maharashtra and Gingee in Tamil Nadu
11 forts, including 10 in Maharashtra and one in Karnataka
13 forts, including two in Tamil Nadu and 11 in Maharashtra
x: The Maratha Military Landscapes comprise 12 forts: 11 in Maharashtra and Gingee in Tamil Nadu. They were inscribed at the 47th session held in Paris in 2025.

s: Which one of the following is the only Harappan site in India included in the UNESCO World Heritage List?
x: Dholavira is the only Harappan site in India included in the UNESCO World Heritage List.

s: Which Indian UNESCO World Heritage Site is in the 'Mixed' category?
x: Khangchendzonga is India's mixed site; Kaziranga is natural, while Khajuraho and Mahabodhi are cultural.

s: Sarnath, inscribed in 2026, became India's which UNESCO World Heritage Site?
x: Sarnath is the 45th; the Maratha Military Landscapes (2025) were the 44th.

s: How many of India's 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites are natural sites?
x: India has 37 cultural, 7 natural and 1 mixed site.

s: Which Indian city was declared a UNESCO World Heritage City in 2019?
x: Ahmedabad became India's first World Heritage City in 2017 and Jaipur, the Pink City, followed in 2019.

s: In which State are the Moidams of the Ahom dynasty, inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2024?
x: The Moidams, mound burials of the Ahom kings, are in Assam and were inscribed in 2024.

s: In which State is the Ramappa Temple, inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2021?
x: Ramappa Temple (2021) is in Telangana; Dholavira, inscribed the same year, is in Gujarat.

s: What is India's rank in the world by number of UNESCO World Heritage Sites (July 2026)?
x: With 45 sites (37 cultural, 7 natural, 1 mixed), India is 6th in the world.

s: Which site of Andhra Pradesh was added to UNESCO's Tentative List of World Heritage Sites in 2022?
o: Sri Veerabhadra Temple and Monolithic Nandi, Lepakshi
x: The Veerabhadra temple and monolithic Nandi at Lepakshi were put on UNESCO's Tentative List in 2022; AP still has no World Heritage Site.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh has a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
2. The Veerabhadra temple at Lepakshi is on UNESCO's Tentative List.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: AP has no World Heritage Site; Lepakshi's Veerabhadra temple and Nandi are only on the Tentative List (2022).

s: In which State are the Nainital and Mussoorie hill stations?
x: Nainital and Mussoorie are in Uttarakhand; Shimla and Manali are in Himachal Pradesh and Darjeeling in West Bengal.

s: Who sculpted the Statue of Unity?
x: The 182 m Statue of Unity at Kevadia, dedicated to Sardar Patel, was sculpted by Ram V. Sutar.

s: Which of the following place–State pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Sarnath (like Kushinagar) is in Uttar Pradesh, not Bihar. Munnar is in Kerala, Mount Abu in Rajasthan and Bodh Gaya in Bihar.

s: Where is the Statue of Unity located?
x: The Statue of Unity is at Kevadia, now also known as Ekta Nagar, in Gujarat.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Munnar is in Kerala, not Tamil Nadu. Alappuzha and Kumarakom are Kerala backwater destinations, Char Dham is associated with Uttarakhand, and Goa is known for beach tourism on the Konkan coast.

s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Char Dham of Uttarakhand?
x: The Char Dham of Uttarakhand comprises Badrinath, Kedarnath, Gangotri and Yamunotri. Rameswaram is not part of this group.

s: Haflong is the only hill station of which State?
x: Haflong is Assam's only hill station.

s: Which is the only hill station in the Aravallis?
x: Mount Abu in Rajasthan is the only hill station in the Aravallis; Auli and Chakrata are in Uttarakhand, Munnar in Kerala.

s: Which of the following beach/hill station – State pairs is correctly matched?
x: Gopnath is in Bhavnagar, Gujarat; Digha is in West Bengal, Munnar in Kerala and Auli in Uttarakhand.

s: Which city is called the yoga capital of India?
x: Rishikesh in Uttarakhand is the yoga capital.

s: Sarnath and Kushinagar are in which State?
x: Sarnath and Kushinagar are in UP; Bodh Gaya is in Bihar.

s: What is the height of the Statue of Unity?
x: The Statue of Unity of Sardar Patel at Kevadia (Ekta Nagar), Gujarat, is 182 m tall.

s: In which State is Auli, a skiing destination, located?
x: Auli in Chamoli district of Uttarakhand is known for skiing.

s: On the bank of which river is the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga at Ujjain?
x: Mahakaleshwar, one of the 12 Jyotirlingas, is at Ujjain (Madhya Pradesh) on the Shipra river.

s: Ahobilam, known for its nine Narasimha shrines, is in which district?
x: Ahobilam, with nine Narasimha shrines, is in Nandyal district.

s: Which temple of Andhra Pradesh has both a Jyotirlinga and a Shakti Peetha?
x: Srisailam has the Mallikarjuna Jyotirlinga and the Bhramaramba Shakti Peetha.

s: The Simhachalam temple is especially noted for which combination of features?
o: Mallikarjuna Jyotirlinga and Bhramaramba Shakti Peetha
Nine Narasimha shrines and a growing Nandi
Satyanarayana Swamy and the Pampa river
Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha, 96 black-stone pillars and the Chandanotsavam tradition
x: Simhachalam is dedicated to Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha, has 96 black-stone pillars, and its idol is uncovered from sandal paste during Chandanotsavam.

s: Srikalahasti temple is associated with which river?
x: Srikalahasti is situated on the Swarnamukhi river.

s: The Annavaram temple stands on which hill?
x: Annavaram is on Ratnagiri hill near the Pampa; Seshachalam is Tirumala, Indrakeeladri is Kanaka Durga and Nallamala is Srisailam.

s: For which of the following is the Veerabhadra temple at Lepakshi famous?
o: a hanging pillar and India's largest monolithic Nandi
nine Narasimha shrines in the Nallamala
a Vayu linga on the Swarnamukhi river
x: Lepakshi (Sri Sathya Sai district) has the hanging pillar, India's largest monolithic Nandi and Vijayanagara murals. The 96 pillars and Chandanotsavam are of Simhachalam, nine Narasimha shrines are at Ahobilam, and the Vayu linga is at Srikalahasti.

s: The Kanaka Durga temple at Vijayawada stands on which hill?
x: Kanaka Durga is on Indrakeeladri; Tirumala is on Seshachalam and Annavaram on Ratnagiri.

s: On which hill does the Tirumala Venkateswara temple stand?
x: Tirumala is on the Seshachalam hills in Tirupati district.

s: In which district is the Yaganti Uma Maheswara temple, known for its growing Nandi?
x: Yaganti, in the Erramala hills, is in Nandyal district.

s: Which hill station of Andhra Pradesh, near Madanapalle in Annamayya district, is called 'Andhra Ooty'?
x: Horsley Hills near Madanapalle (Annamayya) is 'Andhra Ooty'. Lambasingi is the 'Kashmir of Andhra Pradesh', Araku Valley is a coffee and tribal hub (anchor hub), and Maredumilli is a forest area in Polavaram district.

s: Gandikota, called the 'Grand Canyon of India', is a fort on the gorge of which river, in which district?
x: Gandikota fort stands on the Penna (Pennar) gorge in YSR Kadapa district and is one of the seven anchor hubs (heritage, adventure). Krishna/NTR is Kondapalli and Kanaka Durga country; the Godavari gorge has Papikondalu; Tungabhadra/Kurnool is not where Gandikota is.

s: Who found the Borra Caves in 1807?
x: William King George of the GSI found Borra Caves in 1807; Robert Bruce Foote recorded Belum Caves in 1884.

s: By what name is Lambasingi popularly known?
x: Lambasingi in Alluri Sitharama Raju district is called the “Kashmir of Andhra Pradesh” because of its near-freezing winters.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding Borra Caves is correct?
o: They are formed in basalt and contain only stalagmites.
They are karstic limestone caves containing stalactites and stalagmites.
They were first recorded by Robert Bruce Foote in 1884.
They are located in Nandyal district and are the second-longest caves in India.
x: Borra Caves are karstic limestone formations containing stalactites and stalagmites. The 1884 record by Robert Bruce Foote relates to Belum Caves.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Araku Valley — Alluri Sitharama Raju district
x: Maredumilli is in Polavaram district, not Nandyal district. Papikondalu is in the Godavari gorge, Araku Valley is in Alluri Sitharama Raju district and Lambasingi is called the Kashmir of Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which is the highest waterfall in Andhra Pradesh, located in the Sri Venkateswara National Park?
x: Talakona (Tirupati district) in Sri Venkateswara National Park is AP's highest waterfall. Kailasakona is another Tirupati-district waterfall but not the highest; Katiki (near Borra) and Ethipothala (Palnadu) are other AP falls, not the highest.

s: Lepakshi is situated in which district?
x: Lepakshi is situated in Sri Sathya Sai district.

s: Kondapalli Fort is located in which district?
x: Kondapalli Fort is located in NTR district. NTR district also contains Mogalarajapuram and Akkanna Madanna caves.

s: Kondapalli toys of NTR district are made from which soft wood?
x: Kondapalli toys use soft Tella Poniki wood; Etikoppaka toys of Anakapalli use lacquer and natural dyes.

s: Who found the Belum Caves in 1884?
x: Robert Bruce Foote found Belum Caves (1884); William King George found Borra Caves (1807).

s: Thimmamma Marrimanu, the banyan with the largest canopy, is in which district?
x: Thimmamma Marrimanu is in Sri Sathya Sai district.

s: The Buddhist site of Salihundam is in which district?
x: Salihundam is in Srikakulam; Sankaram is in Anakapalli, Guntupalli in Eluru, Bavikonda in Visakhapatnam.

s: The Undavalli rock-cut caves, with a reclining Vishnu, are in which district?
x: Undavalli caves are in Guntur; Kondapalli Fort is in NTR district.

s: Etikoppaka lacquer toys, made with natural dyes, belong to which district?
x: Etikoppaka toys are from Anakapalli; Kondapalli toys are from NTR district.

s: Maredumilli is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Maredumilli is in Polavaram district, not Nandyal.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Buddhist site) - List-II (District)
A. Bavikonda 1. Eluru
B. Sankaram 2. Srikakulam
C. Guntupalli 3. Visakhapatnam
D. Salihundam 4. Anakapalli
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Bavikonda is in Visakhapatnam, Sankaram in Anakapalli, Guntupalli in Eluru and Salihundam in Srikakulam.

s: In which district of Andhra Pradesh is Penukonda fort located?
x: Penukonda, a Vijayanagara stronghold, is in Sri Sathya Sai district, like Lepakshi.

s: Which caves of Andhra Pradesh are the second longest caves in India?
x: Belum Caves in Nandyal district, explored by Robert Bruce Foote in 1884, are the second longest in India.

s: Which of the following initiatives is associated with sustainable and responsible tourism behaviour?
x: Travel for LiFE is the tourism initiative associated with sustainable and responsible travel behaviour.

s: What is the new name of the Travel and Tourism Competitiveness Index?
x: The WEF's Travel and Tourism Competitiveness Index is now the Travel and Tourism Development Index.

s: What is the full form of NIDHI in the tourism sector?
o: National Information Database for Domestic Holidays in India
National Initiative for Domestic Heritage Infrastructure
National Index for Development of Heritage Institutions
National Integrated Database of Hospitality Industry
x: NIDHI stands for National Integrated Database of Hospitality Industry and is a technology-driven database of hospitality and accommodation units maintained by the Ministry of Tourism.

s: Which tourism scheme is associated with the exclusive development of pilgrimage sites?
x: Exclusive pilgrimage-site development is under PRASHAD; Swadesh Darshan (2014–15) is a theme-based circuit scheme and SD 2.0 focuses on sustainable destinations.

s: Which scheme helps States develop iconic tourist centres into global destinations?
x: The Scheme for Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) assists States in developing iconic tourist centres into global destinations.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Incredible India Tourist Facilitator certification — established in 1966
x: ITDC was set up in 1966. Paryatan Didi was launched on 27 September 2024 (2002 is the year of the Incredible India campaign), 1966 belongs to ITDC and not to the Tourist Facilitator certification, and Travel for LiFE is a sustainable, responsible tourism initiative, not a 2014 launch.

s: By what name is the scheme 'Apni Dharohar, Apni Pehchaan' popularly known?
x: ‘Apni Dharohar, Apni Pehchaan’ is the Adopt a Heritage scheme, launched in 2017.

s: What is the full form of PRASHAD?
o: Pilgrimage Restoration and Sustainable Heritage Area Development
Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual, Heritage Augmentation Drive
Public Recreation and Spiritual Heritage Development
Pilgrimage Renewal and Sacred Heritage Development
x: PRASHAD expands to Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual, Heritage Augmentation Drive.

s: How does Swadesh Darshan 2.0 differ from Swadesh Darshan 1.0?
x: SD 2.0 is sustainable and destination-centric; SD 1.0 developed theme-based circuits, and PRASHAD covers only pilgrimage sites.

s: Which of the following tourism campaign/body – year pairs is correctly matched?
x: Incredible India was launched in 2002; ITDC dates from 1966, Adopt a Heritage from 2017 and Swadesh Darshan 1.0 from 2015.

s: In which year was the Adopt a Heritage scheme launched?
x: Adopt a Heritage ('Apni Dharohar, Apni Pehchaan') began in 2017; companies adopt sites to build amenities.

s: In which year was the Swadesh Darshan scheme (1.0) launched?
x: Swadesh Darshan 1.0 for theme-based circuits was launched in 2014-15 (January 2015).

s: With which of the following is the HRIDAY scheme associated?
x: HRIDAY is for heritage city development; PRASHAD is for pilgrimage sites, NIDHI a hospitality database and Adarsh Smarak for model monuments.

s: On which date were the Paryatan Mitra and Paryatan Didi initiatives launched?
x: Paryatan Mitra and Paryatan Didi were launched on 27 September 2024, World Tourism Day.

s: With which State is the Golden Chariot luxury train associated?
x: Golden Chariot is Karnataka's luxury train; Palace on Wheels is Rajasthan and Deccan Odyssey is Maharashtra.

s: MICE tourism is described as which of the following in the context of tourism development?
x: MICE tourism is characterised as high-yield, low-volume tourism and includes meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions.

s: Which country sends the most medical tourists to India?
x: Bangladesh is the top source country for medical tourists to India, whose share in FTAs rose from 2.2% to about 6.5%.

s: Between which places does Ganga Vilas (2023), the world's longest river cruise, run?
x: Ganga Vilas sails from Varanasi to Dibrugarh.

s: Where is the National Maritime Heritage Complex being developed?
x: The National Maritime Heritage Complex is coming up at the Harappan port site of Lothal in Gujarat.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Maritime Heritage Complex:
1. It is being developed at Lothal in Gujarat.
2. It is being developed by the Ministry of Culture.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The complex is at Lothal, but it is being built by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, not the Ministry of Culture.

s: With which country did India sign an MoU in February 2020 for the National Maritime Heritage Complex at Lothal?
x: India signed an MoU with Portugal in February 2020 for the Lothal complex.

s: With which company is India's first submarine tourism project off Dwarka in Gujarat being developed?
x: Gujarat's submarine tourism project off Dwarka is being developed with Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Ltd.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Luxury train) - List-II (State)
A. Palace on Wheels 1. Karnataka
B. Deccan Odyssey 2. Rajasthan
C. Golden Chariot 3. Maharashtra
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Palace on Wheels runs in Rajasthan, Deccan Odyssey in Maharashtra and Golden Chariot in Karnataka.

s: Where is the INS Kursura submarine museum located?
x: INS Kursura, a decommissioned submarine, is a museum on the beach at Visakhapatnam.

s: Which of the following combinations contains only the Andhra Pradesh destinations identified in connection with PRASHAD?
o: Tirupati, Belum Caves, Simhachalam and Polavaram
Srisailam, Belum Caves, Annavaram and Markapuram
Simhachalam, Visakhapatnam Beach Road, Tirupati and Belum Caves
x: The Andhra Pradesh destinations identified in connection with PRASHAD are Tirupati, Srisailam, Simhachalam and Annavaram. Belum Caves is identified separately as a geo-heritage site.

s: Which group of Andhra Pradesh heritage sites is covered under the Adarsh Smarak scheme?
x: Amaravati, Nagarjunakonda and Bavikonda in Andhra Pradesh are covered under Adarsh Smarak.

s: Where is Rushikonda, a certified Blue Flag beach, located?
x: Rushikonda Beach is in Visakhapatnam and is a certified Blue Flag beach.

s: Kotha Koduru, Ramatheertham and Mypadu beaches are associated with which district?
x: Kotha Koduru, Ramatheertham and Mypadu beaches are associated with SPSR Nellore district.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: Mypadu beach is in SPSR Nellore district, not near Machilipatnam. Uppada is in Kakinada district, Yarada in Visakhapatnam and Suryalanka near Bapatla.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Beach) - List-II (Nearest town)
A. Vodarevu 1. Narasapuram
B. Perupalem 2. Machilipatnam
C. Manginapudi 3. Ongole
D. Kothapatnam 4. Chirala
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Vodarevu is near Chirala, Perupalem near Narasapuram, Manginapudi near Machilipatnam and Kothapatnam near Ongole.

s: Suryalanka beach, developed under Swadesh Darshan 2.0, is in which district?
x: Suryalanka beach is near Bapatla; a Rs 97.52 crore Swadesh Darshan 2.0 project is under way there.

s: Which of the following is a Blue Flag beach in Gujarat?
x: Shivrajpur (Gujarat) is a Blue Flag beach; Chandrabhaga is in Odisha and Rushikonda in Andhra Pradesh.

s: Geological heritage sites in India are declared and maintained primarily by which organisation?
o: Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage
x: Geological heritage sites are declared and maintained by the Geological Survey of India, which functions under the Ministry of Mines and has its headquarters at Kolkata.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: Kalinjar Hill is in Banda district of Uttar Pradesh, not Nandyal (Nandyal has Belum Caves). Erra Matti Dibbalu are at Bheemunipatnam, Akal Wood Fossil Park is in Jaisalmer and the Buxa Formation stromatolites are in Sikkim.

s: Belum Caves, declared a geo-heritage site by the GSI in 2025, are in which district?
x: The GSI declared Belum Caves in Nandyal district, AP, a geo-heritage site in 2025.

s: Where is Kalinjar Hill, declared a geo-heritage site in 2026, located?
x: Kalinjar Hill is in Banda (UP), not Nandyal.

s: In which State is the Lonar Lake meteorite crater, a national geo-heritage site?
x: Lonar Lake, a crater formed by a meteorite impact, is in Maharashtra.

s: In which State is the Siwalik Fossil Park located?
x: The Siwalik Fossil Park is in Himachal Pradesh; the Akal Wood Fossil Park is in Rajasthan.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Geo-heritage site) - List-II (State)
A. Pillow lava, Nomira 1. Rajasthan
B. National Fossil Wood Park 2. Odisha
C. Akal Wood Fossil Park 3. Himachal Pradesh
D. Siwalik Fossil Park 4. Tamil Nadu
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Nomira pillow lava is in Odisha, the National Fossil Wood Park at Tiruvakkarai in Tamil Nadu, Akal near Jaisalmer in Rajasthan and Siwalik Fossil Park in Himachal Pradesh.

s: In which State is the pillow lava geo-heritage site of Nomira?
x: The pillow lava at Nomira is a GSI geo-heritage site in Odisha.

s: Where is the National Fossil Wood Park located?
x: The National Fossil Wood Park is at Tiruvakkarai in Tamil Nadu; Akal is near Jaisalmer.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the change in total tourist arrivals in Andhra Pradesh between 2023–24 and 2025–26?
x: Total tourist arrivals rose from 28.58 crore in 2023–24 to 36.42 crore in 2025–26.

s: Andhra Pradesh was ranked which among the States for domestic tourist visits in 2024-25?
x: Andhra Pradesh was the third most visited State for domestic tourism in the cited period.

s: How many beach circuits are identified along Andhra Pradesh's 1,053 km coastline?
x: Five beach circuits are associated with AP's 1,053 km coastline.

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes APTA from APTDC?
o: APTA operates only river cruises, whereas APTDC handles only Buddhist tourism.
APTA handles branding, promotion, investment facilitation and destination management, whereas APTDC operates Haritha hotels, tour packages and boating services.
APTA is the operational State PSU, whereas APTDC is the nodal policy agency.
Both APTA and APTDC are statutory national tourism bodies.
x: APTA is the nodal agency for branding, promotion, investment facilitation and destination management. APTDC is the operational State PSU running Haritha hotels, tour packages, boating and PPP projects.

s: Andhra Pradesh has sought reclassification of Visakhapatnam Beach Road from which CRZ category to which category to facilitate tourism projects?
x: Andhra Pradesh has sought reclassification of Visakhapatnam Beach Road from CRZ-3 to CRZ-2 so that tourism projects can proceed.

s: Which of the following is one of the seven anchor hubs of Andhra Pradesh tourism?
x: The seven anchor hubs are Visakhapatnam, Tirupati, Araku, Rajahmundry, Amaravati, Srisailam and Gandikota; Kakinada is not one.

s: The AP Tourism Policy 2024–29 plans more than how many thematic tourism circuits?
x: The policy plans more than 25 thematic circuits, including Buddhist, temple, beach and river-cruise circuits.

s: Which of the following Andhra Pradesh tourism hub–character pairs is correctly matched?
x: Amaravati is a heritage and Buddhist hub. Tirupati is spiritual, Araku is hill and eco-tourism, and Gandikota is heritage and adventure.

s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Tourism Policy 2024-29, which of the following incentives is offered to tourism projects?
o: Up to 25% fixed capital subsidy and 100% net SGST reimbursement
Up to 50% fixed capital subsidy and 50% SGST reimbursement
Commercial power tariff and full income-tax exemption
Up to 15% fixed capital subsidy only
x: The policy grants industry status and offers up to 25% fixed capital subsidy, industrial power tariff and 100% net SGST reimbursement. The 50%, 15% and income-tax options are not in the policy, and tourism gets the industrial (not commercial) power tariff.

s: Where is the headquarters of the new Polavaram district of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Polavaram district, formed on 31 December 2025, has its headquarters at Rampachodavaram; Markapuram is a separate new district.

s:
Consider the following statements about tourism employment in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Hotels, transport and guides provide direct jobs.
2. Supply-chain jobs are indirect jobs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Direct jobs are in hotels, transport and guiding; supply-chain jobs are indirect.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about centrally protected monuments in India?
o: The AMASR Act was enacted in 1972
The Antiquities and Art Treasures Act was enacted in 1972
x: The AMASR Act dates from 1958; 1972 is the year of the Antiquities and Art Treasures Act.

s: In which year was the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (AMASR) Act passed?
x: The AMASR Act is of 1958; the Antiquities and Art Treasures Act is of 1972.

s: After eleven entry ports were added in August 2026, how many e-Visa checkpoints did India have?
x: Adding eleven ports in August 2026 raised e-Visa checkpoints from 77 to 88.

s: In FY24, travel and tourism accounted for what share of India's GDP?
x: Travel and tourism was 5.22 per cent of GDP in FY24; 13.3 per cent is its share of the workforce.

s: India is the eighth-largest tourism economy. What is its estimated value?
x: India was ranked the eighth-largest tourism economy, valued at approximately US$231.6 billion.

s: How many Foreign Tourist Arrivals (FTAs) did India record in 2024?
x: FTAs in 2024 were 9.95 million. 20.57 million is international tourist arrivals (which include NRIs), 2,947.63 million is domestic tourist visits, and 8.46 crore is the number of tourism jobs, not arrivals.

s: Which State received the most domestic tourist visits in 2024?
x: Uttar Pradesh led with about 646.8 mn domestic visits, followed by Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.

s: Which State received the most foreign tourist visits in 2024?
x: Maharashtra led foreign visits (~3.7 mn), followed by West Bengal.

s: Tourism provides about 8.46 crore jobs, i.e. what share of India's workforce?
x: Tourism jobs are 13.3% of the workforce; 5.22% is tourism's share of GDP (FY24).

s: Which of the following pairs about India's services sector is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Share of India's GVA – More than half
x: India is the 7th largest services exporter, not 3rd; services give more than half of GVA and are the largest FDI recipient.

s: What percentage of urban workers in India are engaged in services?
x: Services employ 62% of India’s urban workers.

s: When was the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) launched?
x: PMJDY was launched on 28 August 2014 and has over 54 crore accounts.

s: What is India's rank among the world's services exporters?
x: India is the 7th largest services exporter, with a 4.3% share of world services exports in 2024 (up from 2% in 2005). 4th, 5th and 10th are not the ranks given.

s: What is the investment in Google's proposed AI data centre at Visakhapatnam and Anakapalli?
x: The AI hub, Google's largest outside the US, has a proposed investment of US$15 billion (about Rs 87,520 crore).

s: With the expansion of which of the following is the spread of IT to Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities mainly associated?
o: STPI units and Global Capability Centres
x: STPI units and Global Capability Centres are spreading IT activity to Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.

s: In which cities does AP's IT and GCC Policy 4.0 (2024-29) plan co-working and neighbourhood workspaces?
x: The policy plans co-working and neighbourhood workspaces in Tirupati, Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada.

s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh had the most bank branches as on 31 December 2024?
x: Visakhapatnam had the most branches (624); Alluri Sitharama Raju had the fewest (52).
